title: Tutorials - House of Pips Wiki
description: Nana's tutorial, which every new career starts with, and Rival School, which teaches seven table styles.
html:
Tutorials

Nana's tutorial #

Nana teaches the rules of her house in eighteen short steps:

  • the bones, their pips and the hammer
  • leading with a double, laying doubles crosswise and spinners
  • matching an open end and rotating a bone onto a vertical branch
  • scoring on multiples of five and counting an open double
  • drawing from the boneyard, blocked hands and winning a hand

Good to know #

  • It is required. Play, Puzzles and Multiplayer stay locked until you finish it once.
  • Finishing the lesson earns the Nana Knows Best achievement. Nana then sits down for a short Old School game with you, first to 75.
  • In the full game and Playtest, Nana's final line invites you to that quick Old School game to 75 points. Read it, then select Finish to start.
  • Complete that match, win or lose, to unlock Old School. Classic Table stays selected for your next game. If you leave the match early, replay Nana's lesson to play it again.
  • Every step works with the mouse, the keyboard or a controller, and the on-screen prompts change to match.
  • In the rotation lesson, select five-six and right-click once. Then click the highlighted top end or drag the rotated bone there. Picking up the same held bone again keeps its orientation.
  • Continue and Finish glow gold when the lesson is ready for you to move on. Boneyard uses the same glow when it is time to draw. With Reduce motion enabled, the glow stays steady.
  • The bone you drew stays visible face up beside Nana while she explains why it does not match and your turn passes.
  • The bone Nana asks for is highlighted after her explanation. Pick it up to reveal the gold placement target; the short instruction changes to the next action as you pick up, rotate and place the bone.
  • Controller focus starts on the requested bone. Back returns it to your rack and restores the pickup instruction.
  • You can replay it from Tutorials > Replay Nana at any time.

Rival School #

Rival School opens after Nana's tutorial. Rival shows you seven table styles, one lesson each: Score Hound, Table Controller, Lock Artist, Counterpuncher, Domino Racer, Pip Shedder and Combo Crafter.

Each lesson sets up a real table, gives you two playable choices, and explains which one the style prefers and why.

  • Show Me and Complete Lesson use the same gold glow when ready.
  • Progress is saved, so you can take the lessons in any order and come back later.
  • Finishing all seven earns the Know Your Rival achievement.
  • See Rival and table styles for what each style wants.
